highlights.sectionIntro: Applied and fundamental research axes organized around a transversal theme: AI and data science for the sustainable development of Haiti and the Caribbean.
highlights.transversalText: Artificial intelligence and data science for the sustainable development of Haiti and the Caribbean

axes.title: Fundamental AI Methods and Machine Learning
axes.description: Developing methods suited to scarce, noisy or heterogeneous data, self-supervised learning, transfer learning, robustness and frugal AI.

axes.title: Computer Vision and Complex Data Analysis
axes.description: Image, document and multimodal data analysis, particularly for agriculture, health, environment and document processing in Haitian Creole and French.

axes.title: Robust, Explainable and Responsible AI
axes.description: Model explainability, algorithmic fairness, bias detection and mitigation, robustness, AI system auditing and evaluation of limitations.

axes.title: AI for Healthcare
axes.description: Medical image analysis, screening and clinical decision support, epidemiological surveillance, documentary assistants and health interfaces in Haitian Creole.

axes.title: AI for Digital Agriculture and Environmental Resilience
axes.description: Crop disease detection, agronomic recommendations, satellite image analysis, early warning systems and climate change adaptation.

axes.title: AI for Socioeconomic, Educational and Institutional Systems
axes.description: Decision support, digital transformation, document automation, Haitian Creole processing and tool development for education, public administration and the economy.

axesDetails.description: This axis forms the laboratory's scientific foundation: it aims to design learning methods that work effectively even when available data is scarce, noisy, or heterogeneous — a common reality in the Caribbean context, where data-collection infrastructure remains limited. The work focuses in particular on self-supervised learning, which makes it possible to exploit unlabeled data, on transfer learning across domains, and on model robustness to variation and bias. Particular attention is paid to computational frugality, to develop high-performing AI without relying on costly infrastructure.

This axis explores the automatic analysis of images, documents, and multimodal data (text, image, signal) for concrete applications in agriculture, health, and the environment. A specific and original dimension of the laboratory concerns the processing of documents written in Haitian Creole and French, a linguistic challenge still poorly covered by existing AI tools. The research combines modern computer-vision techniques with approaches adapted to the local specificities of the data.

Given the growing adoption of AI in sensitive decisions, this axis focuses on making models understandable, fair, and trustworthy. The work covers model explainability, so users can understand the decisions made, the detection and reduction of algorithmic bias, and the auditing of AI systems to assess their limits and risks. This axis is transversal to the others, since it aims to ensure that the solutions developed by the laboratory remain trustworthy and can be deployed responsibly.

This axis applies AI to public-health and clinical challenges, with a focus on medical image analysis for screening support, clinical decision support, and epidemiological surveillance. The laboratory also develops documentary assistants and interfaces for health professionals, designed in Haitian Creole to ease field adoption and meet the real needs of local health systems.

This axis puts AI to work for food security and climate adaptation, two major challenges for the Caribbean region. The research covers automatic detection of crop diseases from images, personalized agronomic recommendations, satellite image analysis for environmental monitoring, and early-warning systems for climate and natural hazards.

This axis explores how AI can support the digital transformation of public and economic institutions. It covers decision support, document automation, and the development of tools adapted to education, public administration, and the local economy, systematically incorporating Haitian Creole processing to ensure the accessibility of the tools developed.

team.sectionTitle: High-level scientific expertise, rooted in Haiti and open to the world
team.sectionIntro: LaCDIA brings together around a dozen complementary scientific and technical profiles — national and international researchers, specialized engineers and emerging-technology experts — to carry out rigorous artificial intelligence research grounded in Caribbean realities.
team.note: Some profiles combine several scientific and institutional responsibilities; this presentation reflects the expertise mobilized by the laboratory rather than a fixed organizational chart.

categories.title: Senior accredited researchers
categories.description: Two national researchers, holders of a Habilitation to Direct Research (HDR), oversee the laboratory's work and ensure its scientific rigor.

categories.title: International scientific network
categories.description: Two international researchers and an emeritus professor complete this scientific core, bringing LaCDIA an outside perspective and established academic collaborations.

categories.title: Associate national researchers
categories.description: Other national researchers, with complementary expertise, are progressively joining the laboratory and contributing to the expansion of its research areas.

categories.title: AI and data engineering
categories.description: Two artificial intelligence engineers, specialized in large-scale data processing, handle the technical implementation of the laboratory's projects and models.

categories.title: Institutional affiliation
categories.description: LaCDIA is affiliated with the École Supérieure d'Infotronique d'Haïti (ESIH), which guarantees its institutional and legal standing. The laboratory's scientific direction is carried out by its own scientific governance bodies.

categories.title: Generative AI expertise
categories.description: A generative artificial intelligence expert completes the team, driving the exploration of these emerging technologies within LaCDIA's work.
